uncertain.note: keying decision, not a doubtful reading: the ANNOTAT. XXVIII margin restarts the alphabet at a, so the page carries TWO notes lettered c — the carry-over one at the head of the page (key 'c', body marker on blocks[0].lines[1]) and this one. Per §4 the second occurrence on the page is keyed c2, in the note and in the body marker on blocks[4].lines[4]. Reader B may well have written {c} for both; reconciler should confirm the rule.

this note has NO marker e anywhere in the body. Every body line of blocks[4] was zoomed at 4x+ and the marker letter is simply not printed. The note is set beside blocks[4].lines[8] ('& de ſoy meſme … interrogué. Voire en'), and that line has an abnormally wide gap between 'interrogué' and its period — almost certainly where the marker e failed to print or fell out. Recorded here so the missing marker e is not read as a transcription omission.

uncertain.text: mangé ſouuẽt, depuis leur enfance auec
uncertain.note: 'ſouuẽt': the mark over the e is a flat, slightly wavy bar (tilde for the omitted n, = ſouuent), NOT the steep acute of 'mangé' on the same line — the two are side by side and clearly different sorts. A careless reading gives 'ſouuét'.

uncertain.note: after 'ce' the print shows TWO marks stacked: a comma on the baseline and, directly above it at ascender height, a small raised comma/apostrophe-shaped stroke. Transcribed as a single comma; the raised mark looks like a stray or doubled sort and cannot be read as a punctuation sign of the period. Zoomed at 5x.

uncertain.note: sic: an unmatched closing parenthesis after 'ici' — no opening parenthesis anywhere on this page. Clearly a paren (tall curved sort), not a comma. Printed with a space before it; closed up per §1. Also 'deſquellesnous' is set solid in the print and divided per §1.

uncertain.note: sic: 'appe-/lè' carries a GRAVE accent (stroke descending left-to-right), not the expected acute of 'appelé'. Checked at 6x. Not corrected.

a small raised horizontal stroke is printed between 'i.' and 'volu.', above the baseline — it does not sit over any letter and is not a legible tilde. Treated as a stray sort and omitted from the line.
'lad.' (= ladite) is set solid as one word with no internal space; kept as printed per the §1 contraction exception rather than divided into 'la d.'.
